query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Low-temperature plasma nitriding treatment of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will form a thin, hardened nitride diffusion layer at the surface that increases surface hardness and wear resistance without compromising the bulk attributes of the alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α + β dual-phase TC4 (Ti6Al4V) alloy with its characteristic low hardness and suboptimal wear performance under high-contact-stress conditions.
generation.intervention: Apply a low-temperature plasma nitriding process, for example at approximately 500°C for 10–20 hours, to encourage nitrogen diffusion into the surface and form surface nitrides.
generation.conditions: Tests performed under ambient to moderately elevated temperatures (up to 500°C) and typical high-stress sliding wear conditions using standard hardness (e.g., Vickers) and pin-on-disk wear tests.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a thin, dense nitrided diffusion layer that includes hard titanium nitride (TiN) phases at the alloy’s surface.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the near-surface region during plasma nitriding, promoting the formation of TiN and other nitrogen-enriched phases that increase the surface hardness and serve as an effective barrier to wear, while the underlying microstructure remains essentially unmodified.
generation.predicted_outcome: A substantial improvement in surface hardness (potentially in the range of a 50–100% increase over untreated TC4) and reduced wear rates compared to the baseline, with the beneficial bulk mechanical properties (like toughness and ductility) maintained.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 alloy exhibiting low hardness and poor friction and wear resistance under extreme-service, high-contact-stress conditions.
generation.boundary: This intervention is applicable under service conditions that replicate high-contact-stress and wear environments and where the plasma nitriding parameters (temperature around 500°C and controlled duration such as 10–20 hours) are strictly maintained.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of improvement in hardness and wear resistance, as well as the potential subtle impacts on fatigue performance, are uncertain without experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of TC4 samples: one set undergoes the low-temperature plasma nitriding treatment as described, and the other remains untreated as a control. Then, perform standardized Vickers hardness testing, pin-on-disk wear testing under high-contact-stress conditions, and fatigue testing to ensure that bulk properties are not degraded.
measurements: Surface hardness (Vickers Hardness Number) at multiple locations on the treated surface
Wear rate or cumulative wear volume from pin-on-disk tests
Fatigue life of both treated and control samples under equivalent loading conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in surface hardness and lower wear rates compared to untreated samples, or if fatigue performance is notably degraded, then the hypothesis is falsified.
